drug_class: Alpha-2 adrenergic agonist / Centrally acting antihypertensive
purpose: Clonidine is most commonly used to treat high blood pressure. It is also used to help with ADHD in children and adults, and sometimes to manage withdrawal symptoms or certain pain conditions. Your doctor may prescribe it for other reasons as well.
how_it_works: Clonidine works in your brain by calming down certain nerve signals that tell your blood vessels to tighten and your heart to beat faster. Think of it like turning down the volume on your body's stress response. This helps your blood vessels relax and your heart rate slow down, which lowers your blood pressure.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include feeling drowsy or sleepy, dry mouth, dizziness, constipation, and headache. You may also feel tired or sluggish, especially when you first start taking it. These effects often get better after your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not stop taking clonidine suddenly without talking to your doctor first — stopping abruptly can cause your blood pressure to spike dangerously high. Be careful when standing up quickly, as it can cause dizziness or lightheadedness. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medication. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, especially other blood pressure medicines or sedatives, as they can interact with clonidine.
typical_dosing: For high blood pressure, a common starting dose is 0.1 mg taken twice a day, morning and night. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose as needed, usually up to 0.2–0.6 mg per day in divided doses. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as dosing can vary depending on what the medication is being used for.
